1. The first eight lines of part (i) do not clearly describe the legitimate users of ORV's on Interior lands. It would appear that operation of an ORV would be permitted by an individual holding neither an operator's or learner's permit if that individual were accompanied by a person 21 years of age or older. This situation poses potentially serious problems related to safety by apparently encouraging the use of ORV's on public lands by unlicensed operators.
2. An operator of an ORV should be required to meet federal licensing regulations that would be uniform throughout all Interior lands open for ORV use. This requirement would eliminate the possibility of ORV use on federal property by individuals meeting inconsistent driving requirements in various states of residence.
3. A serious attempt should be made to license the operator of a specific type of ORV. That an individual can successfully operate an automobile does not guarantee an equal competency in the safe operation of one or several of the many types of ORV's.
